newsitem.title: SYRIA: Assad says Golan destiny decided by people, army.
newsitem.headline: Assad says Golan destiny decided by people, army.

text.p: Syrian President Hafez al-Assad said in a speech published on Friday that the future of the Golan Heights would not be decided by the Israeli occupier.

"Our occupied land and the usurped rights of our nation are our responsibility and our belief in a just and comprehensive peace as a strategic option does not stop us from confronting aggression and occupation," Assad said on Army Day.

"The Arab land is not forlorn for anybody to mess with it. The destiny of the Golan and other Arab land would not be decided by the aggressors and those alien to it but will be decided by the legitimate owners of this land no matter how long it takes."
"The Syrian Arab army has always been since its foundation ready to defend its land and carry out its duties...," Assad added.

Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks on the Golan, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East War, hit total deadlock when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ruled out the withdrawal from the strategic plateau for peace with Syria.
Assad, in his speech, also attacked Netanyahu's government and accused it of "undermining" efforts to revive peace talks between the two countries.

"The Netanyahu government has gone very far in its arrogance and defiance of the international opinion, in its scorn of United Nations resolutions and in its continuing swallowing of Arab lands and building Jewish settlements on them."

"We called for peace...And Israel, under its current government (Likud), responded by going far in extremism and fanaticism, reneged on all that had been achieved during the five years after the start of the peace process and undermined all efforts to revive the process," Assad said.
Previous Israeli Labour government said the scope of any pullback from the Golan would match the kind of ties under peace. Syria demands full withdrawal.
